{"id":"12c142ef-b943-4925-b9a3-335aff867533","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500416,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C7","C9"]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C7","C9"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C7"]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C7"]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C9"]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C9"]},{"requirement_id":"R7","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C7","C9"]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate task requirements against verified claims. We need preserve R1-R7 exactly once. Need assign status fully/partially/unsupported and supported_by claim ids.

We need reason. Original Question asks disorder shared by two cases reported in 2010s, first case in country largest country of dominant religion at establishment, first clinical course, second biopsy symptoms, childhood stiffness then swelling four years later, scientific name. Task skeleton requirements.

Verified claims: all about Stiff person syndrome and FOP. Need see if collectively support each requirement.

R1: "Two reports and their dates" source text: There were two cases in different years that were reported in the 2010s. Claims? C7 and C9 describe case reports of FOP. Do they mention dates/reported in 2010s/different years? No. C7 says 10-year-old Pakistani boy; C9 says sixteen-year-old male. No years or 2010s. C1-C4 about SPS no dates. C5-C11 FOP no report dates. So unsupported? There are two case reports in claims C7 and C9, but requirement specifically "Two reports and their dates" and "reported in the 2010s" and different years. Claims do not establish dates or 2010s. Could partially support existence of two reports? R1 material parts: two cases in different years reported in 2010s. Claims establish two case reports? C7 and C9 are case reports of FOP. But "different years" and "reported in 2010s" not established. The requirement label is "Two reports and their dates", source text. Does C7/C9 count substantive part? They establish two case reports? Maybe "two cases" yes. But "in different years" and "reported in 2010s" no. So partially_supported with C7,C9? Need decide. The definitions: partially_supported if establish at least one substantive material part but not all. The existence of two case reports is a material part. But are C7/C9 the two cases in question? They may be candidate cases. The verified claims mention "A case report of FOP described..." and another "A case report..." These are two reports. They are not necessarily the specific cases from original, but they match symptoms in R4/R5/R6. So likely they are the two cases. R1 asks two reports and dates; claims support two reports but no dates. Thus partially_supported? Need be cautious: The label "Two reports and their dates" includes dates. Claim evidence doesn't include dates. Since the claims do establish two reports (case reports) of FOP. It is substantive part. So partially_supported with C7,C9. But if "two cases in different years reported in 2010s" is entire requirement, only the "two reports" part established. yes partial.

R2: Shared disorder relation. "The cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals." Claims C7 and C9 both are case reports of FOP. Therefore establish both cases are FOP, shared disorder. fully_supported with C7,C9 maybe C5/C6/C8 etc? C7 says case report of FOP; C9 says case report of FOP. So fully_supported supported_by C7,C9. The requirement doesn't ask name? Just shared disorder relation. Yes.

R3: First-case country condition. "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." Claims: C7 says 10-year-old Pakistani boy. Pakistan? Dominant religion Islam, largest Muslim country? Hmm at establishment? Let's parse. "country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." Could be Pakistan? Pakistan was established in 1947 as largest Muslim country? At that time? Actually Pakistan had largest Muslim population? Maybe. C7 mentions Pakistani boy. But does it establish the country was largest country of dominant religion at establishment? No. It only says Pakistani boy. Is "Pakistani" country? It implies patient from Pakistan? It says "Pakistani boy". The requirement: first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at time of its establishment. To support, need country, dominant religion, largest at establishment. C7 only gives Pakistani boy (possibly country). No religion/largest. So maybe partially_supported? It establishes first case individual is Pakistani? But R3 specifically country condition. "The first case was reported in a country..." C7 "Pakistani boy" not explicitly "reported in Pakistan" but likely implies. Does that establish a substantive part: country is Pakistan. But the condition that Pakistan was largest Muslim country at establishment is not established. So partial? Hmm The requirement's material content: first case reported in a country; that country was largest country of its dominant religion in world at time of establishment. C7 gives Pakistani boy, so first case associated with Pakistan? It doesn't say "reported in Pakistan", just Pakistani boy. But we can infer? We must not use outside knowledge. Claim says 10-year-old Pakistani boy. It establishes nationality/ethnicity? Not necessarily location of case report. The requirement "reported in a country" not established. The condition about largest country of religion definitely not. So C7 only supplies "Pakistani boy" maybe not enough. If no support for country condition, unsupported? Let's apply rules: mere entity-name overlap? A "Pakistani boy" is an entity attribute. Does it materially establish "first case was reported in a country that was..."? It partially establishes the country/nationality aspect? It says Pakistani, which is related to country Pakistan. But not the full condition. For partial, need establish at least one substantive material part. "The first case was reported in a country" could be partially supported by "Pakistani boy" if we interpret as Pakistan. But the special condition about dominant religion/largest is unsupported. So partially? We need be strict: Claims establish that a case report described a Pakistani boy. That is at least a material part of identifying the first case's country? Maybe yes, but not the "largest country of dominant religion at establishment" part. I'd mark partially_supported with C7. But is that okay? Need see if any claim about Pakistan being largest Muslim country? No. C7 only Pakistani boy. The requirement source text includes both country and condition. Partial.

R4: First-case clinical course. "In this case, the individual presented with a half-year history of pain in different parts of their body, and the pain gradually worsened, causing difficulty in walking and moving their shoulders." Claim C7 exactly: 10-year-old Pakistani boy presented with 6-month history of pain and tender masses on back, left arm, left hip; pain insidious, gradually worsened, caused difficulty walking and decreased range of motion of shoulders and hips. This fully supports R4. supported_by C7. Maybe also C2 but C2 is general SPS, not specific case. But C7 enough. fully_supported.

R5: Second-case biopsy and symptoms. "In another case, an individual presented complaints of pain and swelling in the upper part of their body, where a procedure involving the collection of tissue samples to test for disease had been performed two months earlier." Claim C9 exactly: sixteen-year-old male presented with complaints of pain and swelling in upper back, where a biopsy had been performed two months before. Fully supported by C9. Note C6 mentions pain/swelling at biopsy site in FOP, but C9 exact. fully_supported C9.

R6: Second-case childhood course. "When they were younger, they had developed stiffness, which was followed by swelling four years later." Claim C9: at age 9, he developed tender stiffness of shoulders and neck, and over next 4 years experienced multiple similar swellings on upper back... This fully supports. supported_by C9. Maybe "followed by swelling four years later" yes.

R7: Requested scientific disorder name. "After evaluating these reports, what is the scientific name of the disorder that both cases were reported to have?" Need establish scientific name. Claims C7 and C9 identify both case reports as fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). C5, C10 etc also. So fully_supported with C7 and C9 (and maybe C5, C6, C8, C10, C11). The requirement asks what is scientific name. C7 and C9 state "case report of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP)" for both cases. So fully_supported. supported_by C7,C9 maybe enough. Could include C5? C5 confirms FOP in a patient by mutation, not necessarily these cases. C10 general FOP. But C7/C9 directly name the disorder for both cases. So fully.

Need decide R1 and R3. Let's re-evaluate.

Task Skeleton R1: "Two reports and their dates" source: "There were two cases in different years that were reported in the 2010s." The requirement likely expects identifying two reports and dates. Verified claims: C7 and C9 describe two case reports but no dates/years. They do establish "two reports" (two case reports). Do they establish "different years"? Not directly. They might be different individuals, but no years. "reported in the 2010s" no. So partially_supported. But supported_by must be claims that establish substantive part. C7 and C9 both are case reports. Yes.

Could R1 be unsupported because "two reports and their dates" is a single requirement with dates central? The definitions: partial if at least one substantive material part. The existence of two reports is substantive. So partial.

R3: "First-case country condition" source: "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." Verified claims: C7 says "A case report of FOP described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy..." Does this establish that the first case was reported in Pakistan? It doesn't explicitly say "reported in Pakistan"; it says Pakistani boy. Could be from Pakistan, but "case report" may be reported elsewhere? However, in medical case reports, "Pakistani boy" often means nationality/country of origin, not necessarily where reported. But the requirement includes "country that was the largest country of its dominant religion..." Which country? If we use outside knowledge, Pakistan is an Islamic republic, largest Muslim country? But cannot. Claim does not mention dominant religion or largest. So only "Pakistani" aspect. Is that a substantive material part of "first-case country condition"? It identifies the country (Pakistan) as associated with the first case. But not the condition. Partial. If strict, maybe unsupported because the requirement is the condition about the country, not just country identity. The condition is "country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." The claim "Pakistani boy" doesn't establish any part of that condition? It establishes the country is Pakistan? Actually the condition has predicate: "was the largest country of its dominant religion..." The first part "first case was reported in a country" is supported? C7 doesn't say reported in Pakistan, but "Pakistani boy" likely. Hmm.

Let's parse the requirement: "First-case country condition." The source span: "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." Material conditions:
1. first case was reported in a country.
2. that country was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment.

C7 establishes first case is about a Pakistani boy. Does that establish the first case was reported in a country? It implies the case report described a Pakistani boy; not necessarily "reported in Pakistan." But at least the patient is Pakistani. It doesn't establish the country condition. There is no claim about country being largest country of dominant religion. So at best partial if we count "Pakistani" as country part. But the "country condition" is the whole predicate. Could be unsupported because no claim establishes that the country was largest country of its dominant religion. The definition for partially: establish at least one substantive material part. Is "Pakistani boy" a substantive part of "first case was reported in a country that was largest..."? It identifies a country/nationality. The requirement isn't just "country"; it's "country that was largest..." The material part "reported in a country" is generic, but the special condition is the core. I'd lean partially_supported because C7 provides the country (Pakistan) but not the religious/largest condition. Need output supported_by C7.

R2: shared disorder relation. C7 and C9 both FOP. fully.

R7: scientific name. fully with C7,C9. Could include C5/C10? But direct.

Need ensure no requirement omitted. R1-R7.

Let's consider if claims C7/C9 actually are the two cases in question. They match R4/R5/R6 exactly. The first case is C7: 10-year-old Pakistani boy, 6-month history pain, etc. Second C9: 16-year-old male, pain/swelling upper back, biopsy two months before, age 9 stiffness, over next 4 years swellings. These match original. So they are the two cases. The shared disorder is FOP. The original asks scientific name; FOP is fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. Claims C7/C9 call it FOP. C5/C10 expand FOP. So R7 fully supported.

Now, R1: "There were two cases in different years that were reported in the 2010s." The claims don't mention years. Are there any dates? C7: 10-year-old; C9: sixteen-year-old, age 9. No report years. So partial? It establishes two cases. But "reported in 2010s" and "different years" not established. Could the fact that C7 and C9 are case reports in medical literature imply they were reported? But not years. So partial.

R3: "first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." C7 says Pakistani boy. Does it establish Pakistan? The claim uses "Pakistani" as adjective. It does not state Pakistan was largest country of dominant religion. So partial.

Could R3 be fully_supported if we use outside knowledge? No outside. No.

Potential issue: We must "Do not use outside knowledge." So cannot infer Pakistan's religion/largest. Thus not fully. Can we infer "Pakistani" means from Pakistan? That's linguistic, not outside. So partial.

Could R3 be unsupported because the specific condition "largest country of its dominant religion" is not established at all, and "Pakistani boy" is not a material part of that condition? The requirement is "First-case country condition", not "first-case patient nationality". The condition is about country's religious demographic status. The claim doesn't establish any of that. If we treat the requirement as a whole, it asks for a country that meets a property. The claim only gives a nationality adjective; it does not establish the country meets property. The material part "first case was reported in a country" is not even explicitly established. Hmm. In these tasks, partial support often if some but not all parts. The country identity could be considered a part. I think partial is safer. But let's examine examples? No examples.

Need decide final JSON. It should be valid JSON only. Include supported_by arrays. For unsupported empty array.

Maybe R1 also could be unsupported because "dates" is central and no dates. But two reports are established. The label "Two reports and their dates" includes two reports. So partial.

R2 fully supported by C7,C9. Should we include C5? C5 says confirmed FOP in a patient; not necessarily both. C7 and C9 are enough.

R4 fully C7.

R5 fully C9.

R6 fully C9.

R7 fully C7,C9. Maybe include C5? The requirement asks scientific name of disorder both cases reported to have. C7 and C9 name FOP. C5 gives full name? Actually C5 says "Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) was confirmed..." C7 says "case report of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP)" already full. C9 says "FOP" but C7 gives full name. So C7 alone plus C9 relation. Use C7,C9.

Need ensure JSON schema exactly. "requirements": [ ... ].

Let's think if R1 should include C7,C9? They are case reports of FOP. They don't have dates. Could C9 mention "sixteen-year-old male", "at age 9", "over next 4 years" not report date. C7 "10-year-old Pakistani boy". No.

R3: supported_by C7? C7 says Pakistani boy. If we mark partially_supported, supported_by must include C7. If we mark unsupported, empty. Which is more appropriate? Let's revisit definitions:
- partially_supported: Verified Claims establish at least one substantive material part of the requirement, but one or more material parts remain unsupported.
- unsupported: Verified Claims do not establish any substantive material part. Mere topical relevance, entity-name overlap, candidate mention, prior search direction, or background context does not count as support.

R3 requires: "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment."
Material parts:
a) first case was reported in a country.
b) that country was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment.

Does C7 establish (a)? It says "A case report of FOP described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy..." This does not say the case was reported in Pakistan. It describes a Pakistani boy. It might imply the case report was about a Pakistani boy, but not necessarily reported in Pakistan. However, "Pakistani boy" is an entity in the case; it establishes nationality. Does that establish "reported in a country"? Not exactly. But the country condition is about the country where the case was reported. If the boy is Pakistani, likely the case was from Pakistan, but not explicitly. Could be a Pakistani boy living elsewhere. So even (a) not fully. But maybe we can consider "Pakistani boy" as identifying Pakistan as the country of the first case. It's a substantive part. Hmm.

If we are strict, C7 does not establish the country of report, nor the religious largest condition. So unsupported? But then R3 would be unsupported despite C7 having "Pakistani". Is that "mere entity-name overlap"? The requirement mentions "country"; C7 mentions "Pakistani" (derived from country). That could be entity-name overlap. The rule says mere entity-name overlap does not count. So if only Pakistani is mentioned, it might not count as support for the country condition. But it's more than overlap: it identifies the first case individual as Pakistani. However, the requirement is about the country being largest Muslim country at establishment. No claim about that. The core condition is unsupported. The requirement's label "First-case country condition" might mean the condition itself, not just country identity. So maybe unsupported. But then partial support would require at least one substantive material part. Is "Pakistani" a substantive part of the condition? The condition is "country that was the largest country of its dominant religion..." It is a predicate about the country. The identity of the country (Pakistan) is part of it. C7 establishes the country is Pakistan? If yes, then partial. But if not explicit, maybe not.

Let's look at original question: "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." The country is Pakistan? The first case is C7: Pakistani boy. The country condition likely is Pakistan was the largest Muslim country at the time of its establishment? Actually Pakistan established 1947, was it largest Muslim country? At that time, Pakistan had largest Muslim population? Let's use outside: Pakistan was created as a homeland for Muslims, but at establishment, maybe it was the largest Muslim country? Actually Indonesia is largest Muslim country now, but in 1947 Indonesia was independent? Indonesia declared independence 1945, population maybe larger. Pakistan at 1947 had 75 million? Indonesia had 70? Hmm uncertain. Maybe the country is "Pakistan" and dominant religion Islam. But verified claims don't say that.

In the evidence, C7 says Pakistani boy. So it gives the country as Pakistan. But no claim about religion/largest. So partial. I think partial is acceptable.

R1: "Two reports and their dates" C7/C9 establish two reports but no dates. Partial. If strict, dates are material, but two reports are material. yes.

Could R2 be partially supported if both cases are FOP but not "shared disorder relation"? They both have FOP, so fully.

Let's prepare final JSON. Need ensure no extra text. The final answer should be JSON object. Use exact statuses.

I'll include R1 partial with C7,C9. R3 partial with C7. Others as above.

Double-check if R2 should include C5? No.

Let's consider if R7 should include C5 and C10 for scientific name? C7 states "fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP)" which is the scientific name. C9 states "FOP". So C7 and C9 collectively name disorder for both cases. C7 gives full name. Good.

Potential alternative: R1 unsupported because no dates. But partial due two reports. If the grading expects exact, uncertain. Let's reason from definitions: A requirement is not just label; source span is "There were two cases in different years that were reported in the 2010s." The material conditions: (i) two cases exist; (ii) in different years; (iii) reported in 2010s. Claims establish two case reports (C7,C9). They do not establish different years or 2010s. So partial. Yes.

R3: source span: "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." Material conditions: (i) first case reported in a country; (ii) that country was largest country of its dominant religion in world at establishment. Claims: C7 "A case report of FOP described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy..." Does it establish first case reported in a country? It doesn't explicitly say "reported in Pakistan", but it describes a Pakistani boy. Could count as establishing the first case involved a Pakistani individual. The requirement is about country condition. It gives the country as Pakistan (via nationality). So partial. If we are very strict, maybe unsupported. Which would be more aligned with "Do not infer a fact merely because entity, event, document, date, role, relation, or attribute is mentioned by Task Skeleton"? The claim mentions Pakistani boy. The requirement mentions country. We can infer the country is Pakistan? That's linguistic. But the requirement's condition is not established. I think partial is nuanced.

Let's see if there is any claim about "largest country of its dominant religion" in C1-C11? No. So R3 cannot be fully or partially? Partial if country identity counts. The requirement's label "First-case country condition" maybe specifically the condition, not the country identity. But source span includes "reported in a country that was the largest country..." The existence of a country is part. C7 gives Pakistani. So partial.

I'll final with partial for R1 and R3.
